name: split_additional_suffix_basic
cmd_target: BINARY --lines=2 --additional-suffix=.txt in && cat xaa.txt && echo --- && cat xab.txt && echo --- && cat xac.txt

name: split_lines_basic
description: split --lines=2 splits a 5-line input into 3 files (xaa,xab,xac); xad must not exist
cmd_target: BINARY --lines=2 in && cat xaa && echo --- && cat xab && echo --- && cat xac && test ! -f xad && echo NOXAD

name: split_n_more_than_size
cmd_target: BINARY -n 10 /dev/null && stat -c %s x* | uniq -c | sed 's/^ *//; s/ /x/'

name: split_n4_abc
description: split -n 4 of 'abc' yields a, b, c, empty
cmd_target: BINARY -n 4 abc && cat xaa && echo --- && cat xab && echo --- && cat xac && echo --- && stat -c %s xad && test ! -f xae && echo NOXAE

name: split_n2_abc
cmd_target: BINARY -n 2 abc && cat xaa && echo --- && cat xab && test ! -f xac && echo NOXAC

name: split_n_kn_zero_input
cmd_target: BINARY -n 2/3 /dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x?? 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_elide_n_zero_input
cmd_target: BINARY -e -n 10 /dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x?? 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_fail_a_zero
description: split -a 0 succeeds (suffix length 0 allowed on empty input)

name: split_C_no_empty
description: split -C 1 on a single-byte input creates 2 files, no third
cmd_target: echo x | BINARY -C 1; test -f xaa && test -f xab && echo TWO; test -f xac && echo BAD || echo OK

name: split_huge_obsolete_n
description: split with a huge obsolete -N succeeds

name: split_filter_xz
description: split --filter='xz -1 > $FILE.xz' produces compressed segments that round-trip
cmd_prep: command -v xz >/dev/null || exit 77; rm -f in out out-* && seq 5 > in
cmd_target: BINARY -l2 --filter='xz -1 > $FILE.xz' in out- && xz -dc out-* > out && diff in out && echo OK

name: split_filter_elide_empty
description: split -e -n 10 --filter creates no files when nothing to write
cmd_target: BINARY -e -n 10 --filter='xz > $FILE.xz' /dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x?? 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_guard_input_regular
description: split -C 6 on its own input must fail (no overwrite)
cmd_prep: rm -f x* in2 in3 exp-1 && seq 10 | tee exp-1 > xaa && ln -s xaa in2 && ln xaa in3

name: split_guard_input_symlink
description: split -C 6 on a symlink to its own input must fail
cmd_prep: rm -f x* in2 in3 exp-1 && seq 10 | tee exp-1 > xaa && ln -s xaa in2 && ln xaa in3

name: split_guard_input_hardlink
description: split -C 6 on a hardlink to its own input must fail
cmd_prep: rm -f x* in2 in3 exp-1 && seq 10 | tee exp-1 > xaa && ln -s xaa in2 && ln xaa in3

name: split_guard_input_stdin_redirect
description: split -C 6 - reading from its own input must fail
cmd_prep: rm -f x* in2 in3 exp-1 && seq 10 | tee exp-1 > xaa && ln -s xaa in2 && ln xaa in3

name: split_lchunk_invalid_chunks
description: split -n l/1o reports invalid chunk count

name: split_lchunk_empty_input
description: split -n l/1 on empty input creates a single empty xaa
cmd_target: : | BINARY -n l/1 && stat -c %s xaa && test ! -f xab && echo NOXAB

name: split_lchunk_more_than_size
description: split -n l/10 of /dev/null creates 10 zero-sized files
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/10 /dev/null && stat -c %s x* | uniq -c | sed 's/^ *//; s/ /x/'

name: split_lchunk_elide_empty
description: split -e -n l/10 of /dev/null creates no files
cmd_target: BINARY -e -n l/10 /dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x?? 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_lchunk_invalid_chunk_number
description: split -n l/16/15 reports invalid chunk number
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/16/15 in 2>&1 | sed "s/': .*/'/"; echo done

name: split_lchunk_extract_13_15
description: split -n l/13/15 yields empty output for given input
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/13/15 in > out && stat -c %s out

name: split_lchunk_extract_14_15
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/14/15 in > out && cat out

name: split_lchunk_extract_15_15
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/15/15 in > out && cat out

name: split_lchunk_no_eol
description: split -n l/7/7 on input lacking trailing newline yields '5'
cmd_target: BINARY -n l/7/7 in > out && cat out

name: split_line_bytes_basic
description:
split -C5 of '1
2222
3
4' produces correct chunk sizes

name: split_line_bytes_no_eol
description: split -C5 of '0123456789' (no eol) splits into 2 files of size 5,5
cmd_prep: rm -f in x* && seq 0 9 | tr -d '\n' > in

name: split_line_bytes_holdbuf
description: split -C 131072 splits a large file into expected segment sizes
cmd_prep:
rm -f bigin x* && printf '%131070s
' '' > a && printf 'x
' > b && printf '%131071s
' '' > c && cat a b c > bigin && rm -f a b c
cmd_target: BINARY -C 131072 ---io=131072 bigin && stat -c %s xaa xab xac | paste -s -d ' '

name: split_numeric_basic
cmd_target: BINARY --numeric-suffixes --lines=2 in && cat x00 && echo --- && cat x01 && echo --- && cat x02

name: split_numeric_start_9
cmd_target: BINARY --numeric-suffixes=9 --lines=2 in && cat x09 && echo --- && cat x10 && echo --- && cat x11

name: split_hex_basic
cmd_target: BINARY --hex-suffixes --lines=2 in && cat x00 && echo --- && cat x01 && echo --- && cat x02

name: split_hex_start_9
cmd_target: BINARY --hex-suffixes=9 --lines=2 in && cat x09 && echo --- && cat x0a && echo --- && cat x0b

name: split_rchunk_more_than_size
description: split -n r/10 of /dev/null creates 10 zero-sized files
cmd_target: BINARY -n r/10 /dev/null && stat -c %s x* | uniq -c | sed 's/^ *//; s/ /x/'

name: split_rchunk_elide_empty
description: split -e -n r/10 on /dev/null creates no files
cmd_target: BINARY -e -n r/10 /dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x?? 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_rchunk_basic
cmd_target: BINARY -n r/3 in && cat xaa && echo --- && cat xab && echo --- && cat xac

name: split_rchunk_select_2_3
description: split -n r/2/3 extracts the 2nd round-robin chunk
cmd_target: BINARY -n r/2/3 in > out && cat out

name: split_rchunk_no_trailing_nl
description: split -n r/2/3 with input missing trailing newline

name: split_record_sep_lines
description: split -t : --lines=2 with custom separator produces correct chunks
cmd_target: BINARY --lines=2 -t : in && cat xaa && echo === && cat xab && echo === && cat xac

name: split_record_sep_no_arg
description: split -t with no argument must fail

name: split_suffix_auto_off_when_start
description: split -b1 --numeric=89 fails (auto-widening off when start specified) for 12-byte file
cmd_target: BINARY file.in -b1 --numeric=89 2>/dev/null; echo exit=$?; ls x* 2>/dev/null | wc -l

name: split_suffix_auto_widen
description: split -b1 --numeric on 91-byte file auto-widens (creates x89 and x9000)
cmd_target: BINARY file.in -b1 --numeric && test -e x89 && test -e x9000 && echo OK

name: split_suffix_auto_widen_with_addsuffix
cmd_target: BINARY file.in -b1 --numeric --additional-suffix=.txt && test -e x89.txt && test -e x9000.txt && echo OK

name: split_suffix_no_auto_with_number_high_start
description: split --numeric-suffixes=100 --number=r/100 must fail (no auto when start>=N)

name: split_suffix_length_too_short
cmd_target: BINARY -b 1 -a 1 in 2>&1; echo exit=$?; test -f xa && test -f xz && echo HEADTAIL; test -f xaa && echo BAD || echo OK

name: split_suffix_length_ok
cmd_target: BINARY --verbose -b 1 -a 2 in && test ! -f xbb && echo NOXBB && cat xaa xab xaz xba 2>/dev/null

name: split_suffix_length_a2_n_too_large
description: split -a2 -n1000 on /dev/null fails (n too large for suffix)
cmd_target: BINARY -a2 -n1000 < /dev/null 2>/dev/null; echo exit=$?; test -f xaa && echo BAD || echo OK
